sections.text:
World action models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic control by jointly predicting future visual dynamics and actions from an initial observation and instruction. However, existing WAMs struggle with long-horizon prediction, as generating dense video rollouts is highly inefficient.

Some recent WAMs address this by predicting a single future frame without generating the full video, but this approach neglects how to progress toward the goal.

We present ProWAM, a progressive world action model that jointly predicts actions and an ordered sequence of sparse visual sub-goals, providing explicit visual guidance to anchor action generation throughout task execution.

This design scales naturally, as sub-goal prediction can be learned from large-scale action-free videos, allowing the video backbone to offload complex visual planning from the action policy.

For efficient action generation, ProWAM executes a single video-backbone forward pass to cache sparse sub-goal features, eliminating iterative full-video generation and requiring only lightweight action denoising during replanning. Across extensive evaluations, ProWAM achieves superior out-of-distribution robustness.

On simulation benchmarks, it sets new state-of-the-art results on LIBERO-Plus (85.8%) and randomized RoboTwin (75.7%), outperforming the strongest baseline with relative gains of up to +35.9%.On RoboCasa365, ProWAM achieves a 48.1% success rate and 18.2% on the challenging Composite-Unseen split, ranking 4th overall.

Crucially, in zero-shot real-world experiments, ProWAM achieves 70.0% success, outperforming the strongest baseline by +15.0 (from 55.0% to 70.0%, a +27.3% relative gain) in novel scenes. These results demonstrate the value of progress-indexed visual foresight for closed-loop control. Our program is in https://sii-ferenas.github.io/ProWAM-page.

summary.en: The paper presents ProWAM, a progressive world action model that jointly predicts actions and an ordered sequence of sparse visual sub-goals to guide action generation during task execution. It proposes learning sub-goal prediction from action-free videos and caching sub-goal features with one video-backbone forward pass, followed by lightweight action denoising during replanning. The authors report results on simulation benchmarks and zero-shot real-world experiments, limited to the described evaluation settings.
summary.zh: 论文提出渐进式世界动作模型 ProWAM，联合预测动作与有序的稀疏视觉子目标，为任务执行中的动作生成提供视觉指引。模型可借助无动作标注视频学习子目标，并通过一次视频骨干前向计算缓存其特征，以轻量动作去噪支持重规划。作者报告其在多个仿真基准上的表现及零样本真实世界实验结果；这些结果限于所述评测设置。

items.title: World Action Modeling with Progressive Visual Planning

sections.text:
Robotic locomotion is often approached with the goal of maximizing robustness and reactivity by increasing motion control frequency. We challenge this intuitive notion by demonstrating robust and dynamic locomotion with a learned motion controller executing at as low as 8 Hz on a real ANYmal C quadruped.

The robot is able to robustly and repeatably achieve a high heading velocity of 1.5 m/s, traverse uneven terrain, and resist unexpected external perturbations. We further present a comparative analysis of deep reinforcement learning (RL) based motion control policies trained and executed at frequencies ranging from 5 Hz to 200 Hz.

We show that low-frequency policies are less sensitive to actuation latencies and variations in system dynamics. This is to the extent that a successful sim-to-real transfer can be performed even without any dynamics randomization or actuation modeling. We support this claim through a set of rigorous empirical evaluations.

Moreover, to assist reproducibility, we provide the training and deployment code along with an extended analysis at https://articulated.robots.ox.ac.uk/lfmc/.

summary.en: The paper studies learned low-frequency motion control and reports deployment at rates as low as 8 Hz on a real ANYmal C quadruped. The authors say the robot repeatedly reaches a high heading velocity, crosses uneven terrain, and resists unexpected external perturbations. They compare deep reinforcement learning policies trained and executed at frequencies from 5 to 200 Hz, reporting that low-frequency policies are less sensitive to actuation latency and changes in system dynamics. They also report sim-to-real transfer without dynamics randomization or actuation modeling.
summary.zh: 论文研究低频运动控制，并报告一款真实 ANYmal C 四足机器人使用最低 8 Hz 的学习控制器实现运动。作者称机器人能够重复达到较高航向速度、通过不平地形并抵抗意外外力。论文还比较了训练和执行频率为 5 至 200 Hz 的深度强化学习策略，报告低频策略对执行延迟和系统动力学变化较不敏感，并称在未采用动力学随机化或执行器建模时也完成了仿真到现实迁移。

items.title: Learning Low-Frequency Motion Control for Robust and Dynamic Robot Locomotion

sections.text:
Adversarial patches can disrupt Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by manipulating visual observations, leading to failures in robot control. However, it remains poorly understood which internal mechanisms underlie these failures and how targeted interventions can mitigate them.

In this work, we mechanistically analyze VLA representations using a sparse autoencoder (SAE) and identify a feature whose activation strongly correlates with the presence of an adversarial patch. Based on this analysis, we suppress the identified feature at inference time only when a linear probe detects an attack.

This intervention improves robustness without the cost of fine-tuning the VLA. We evaluate our method against VLA adversarial patch attacks on LIBERO-10.Conditional intervention improves success rate under intermittent attacks, whereas continuously applying the same intervention substantially degrades policy performance.

These results show that attack-related internal representations can provide useful targets for VLA adversarial defense and that controlling when to intervene is important for limiting disruption to nominal policy behavior.

summary.en: The paper analyzes mechanisms behind adversarial patch failures in vision-language-action models. Using a sparse autoencoder, the authors identify a feature whose activation strongly correlates with a patch, then suppress it at inference only when a linear probe detects an attack. Evaluated against attacks on LIBERO-10, the intervention requires no VLA fine-tuning. The authors report improved success under intermittent attacks with conditional intervention, while continuously applying it substantially degrades policy performance.
summary.zh: 论文分析视觉语言动作模型对抗贴片攻击的内部机制，使用稀疏自编码器识别出一个与贴片存在强相关的特征，并在推理时仅于线性探针检测到攻击时抑制该特征。作者在 LIBERO-10 上评估这一无需微调模型的干预，报告条件式干预可提升间歇攻击下的成功率，而持续干预会明显降低策略表现。研究据此指出，攻击相关内部表征可用于防御，干预时机也会影响正常策略行为。

items.title: Detect and Suppress: A Mechanistic Defense against Adversarial Patches in VLA Models

sections.text:
Vision language model (VLM) agents can control robots through visual feedback and action primitives, but repeated model invocations and redundant observations incur substantial token overhead.

We introduce PyRUA-Lean, an interactive code-execution framework that couples feedback-driven primitive composition with selective observation: the agent composes classical robot primitives and learned vision-language-action (VLA) policies into Python cells that perform conditional checks and local retries, returning only explicitly requested images and state feedback for replanning.

Across 700 simulated task instances from LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboCasa365, we compare PyRUA-Lean with a tool-calling baseline using the same GPT-6 Astra planner and underlying robot primitives. Under equal LLM-call budgets, PyRUA-Lean increases overall success from 63.1% to 71.7%.

On instances solved by both agents, it uses 49% fewer LLM calls and 65% fewer input tokens.

summary.en: The paper introduces PyRUA-Lean, a code-execution framework in which an agent composes classical robot primitives and learned vision-language-action policies into Python cells. These cells perform conditional checks and local retries, returning selectively requested images and state feedback for replanning. In 700 simulated task instances across LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboCasa365, the authors compare it with a tool-calling baseline using the same planner and primitives. They report higher overall success under equal call budgets and fewer calls and input tokens on instances solved by both agents.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PyRUA-Lean，让智能体将传统机器人动作原语与学习型视觉语言动作策略组合成可执行的 Python 单元，进行条件检查和局部重试，并选择性返回图像及状态反馈以供重规划。作者在 LIBERO-PRO、RoboTwin 2.0 和 RoboCasa365 的 700 个仿真任务实例上，与使用相同规划器和动作原语的工具调用基线比较；在相同模型调用预算下，报告总体成功率提高，并在双方均解决的实例上减少调用和输入词元。

items.title: Fewer Tokens, Better Action: GPT-6 Astra Robot Agents with 14% Higher Success Rate but 65% Fewer Tokens

sections.text:
Physics simulators and motion planners require convex collision geometry, yet image-to-3D generative models output dense, frequently non-manifold visual meshes. Bridging the two today takes a slow, brittle reconstruct-then-decompose pipeline of repair, decimation, and approximate convex decomposition.

We present I2CD, which predicts a convex decomposition directly from a single RGB image.

Rather than train a new image-to-3D model, I2CD freezes the pretrained Hunyuan3D-2 image-conditioned diffusion transformer and shape decoder and trains only a lightweight cross-attention head (38M parameters, under ten GPU-hours) whose learned "convex-slot" tokens emit the halfplane parameters of $K$ convex polytopes.

The output is compact, convex by construction, and loads into physics engines without any post-processing, in ${\sim}0.5$s per image. On $227$ held-out OmniObject3D and Google Scanned Objects instances, I2CD attains the highest volumetric IoU among eight reconstruct-then-decompose pipelines while running $6$-$37\times$ faster end-to-end.

In a cross-simulator study in MuJoCo, PyBullet, Genesis, and Isaac Sim, every engine uses I2CD geometry as delivered, whereas raw generated meshes "load" everywhere but are silently replaced by a different collision shape in most cases or need seconds to minutes of per-object preprocessing.

On a physical xArm7, I2CD produces planner-ready geometry for a $20$-object cluttered scene in $11$s versus $328$s for the strongest baseline, at comparable pick-and-place execution success ($85$ vs. $90$ of $100$ trials).

summary.en: I2CD predicts a convex decomposition directly from one RGB image by training a lightweight cross-attention head while freezing a pretrained image-conditioned model and shape decoder. Its output consists of convex polytopes defined by halfplane parameters. On 227 held-out instances, the authors report the highest volumetric IoU among eight reconstruct-then-decompose pipelines and 6–37× faster end-to-end runtime. In four simulators, the geometry is used as delivered. On an xArm7 physical setup, preparing a 20-object scene took 11 seconds; pick-and-place succeeded in 85 of 100 trials, compared with 90 for the baseline.
summary.zh: I2CD提出从单张RGB图像直接预测凸分解，以满足物理仿真器和运动规划器对凸碰撞几何的需求。该方法冻结预训练的图像条件模型与形状解码器，仅训练轻量交叉注意力头，输出由半平面参数定义的凸多面体。在227个留出实例上，作者报告其体积IoU高于八种先重建再分解的流程，端到端速度快6至37倍。MuJoCo、PyBullet、Genesis和Isaac Sim均直接使用其几何；xArm7实验中，20物体场景的规划几何生成用时11秒，100次抓放成功85次，基线为328秒和90次。

items.title: I2CD: Direct Image-to-Convex Decomposition for Simulation-Ready Collision Geometry

sections.text:
Imitation learning for contact-rich manipulation requires high-quality expert data that is expensive to obtain. This makes learning a sample-efficient policy a key issue. To address this, we propose VISTA, a workspace-level equivariant visuotactile diffusion policy for data-efficient contact-rich imitation learning.

VISTA projects visual and tactile observations into spherical tokens, injects tactile contact cues into visual spherical directions through permutation-equivariant spherical fusion, and rotates the fused harmonic representation using the end-effector orientation.

The resulting representation conditions an equivariant diffusion policy to predict spatially consistent actions. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world robotic settings show that VISTA substantially improves data efficiency over strong visuotactile imitation learning baselines. Project website: https://vista-paper.github.io/

summary.en: VISTA is a workspace-level equivariant visuotactile diffusion policy for data-efficient imitation learning in contact-rich manipulation. It projects visual and tactile observations into spherical tokens, fuses tactile contact cues into visual spherical directions, and rotates the fused harmonic representation according to end-effector orientation. This representation conditions a diffusion policy to predict spatially consistent actions. The authors report that experiments in simulation and real-world robotic settings show substantially improved data efficiency over strong visuotactile imitation-learning baselines.
summary.zh: VISTA是一种面向接触丰富操作、强调数据效率的工作空间级等变视觉触觉扩散策略。它将视觉和触觉观测投影为球面令牌，通过置换等变球面融合把触觉接触线索注入视觉球面方向，再依据末端执行器姿态旋转融合后的调和表示。该表示用于条件化扩散策略，以预测空间一致的动作。作者称，在仿真和真实机器人实验中，VISTA相较于强视觉触觉模仿学习基线显著提高了数据效率。

items.title: Equivariant Visual-Tactile Diffusion Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation

sections.text:
In lifelong reinforcement learning, retaining previously learned policies is not sufficient for effective transfer to a new task. Useful knowledge may be distributed across several prior policies, and its relevance may change as the learner acquires experience.

One hypothesis is that task similarity can be effectively used in a continual learning setting to find and combine previously learned policies. To test it, Adaptive Mask Selection and Composition (AMSC) is designed to estimate similarity from online experience via non-parametric Wasserstein task embeddings from state-action-reward samples.

The z-score-normalized sparsemax of the similarity scores are used to derive a variable-size support to periodically choose and weight policies to form a prior when learning a new task. On CT-graph and MiniGrid, AMSC achieves higher mean performance and forward transfer than the evaluated modular composition baselines while exhibiting no forgetting.

Results on Continual World suggest that identifying relevant prior knowledge and determining its layer-specific composition may require additional layer-specific tuning. Ablations show that selecting relevant sources and determining how strongly to reuse them are central to these gains.

Independently measured pairwise transfer is also positively associated with task-embedding similarity. These results indicate that task similarity can be an effective criterion to select and weight specific knowledge for reuse in lifelong reinforcement learning.

summary.en: AMSC estimates task similarity from online state-action-reward samples using non-parametric Wasserstein task embeddings. It applies z-score-normalized sparsemax scores to periodically select and weight a variable set of prior policies as a learning prior for a new task. On CT-graph and MiniGrid, the authors report higher mean performance and forward transfer than evaluated modular composition baselines, with no forgetting. Results on Continual World suggest layer-specific tuning may be needed. Ablations indicate that both selecting useful sources and setting their reuse strength contribute to the reported gains.
summary.zh: AMSC研究如何在终身强化学习中根据在线经验寻找并组合已有策略。它从状态、动作和奖励样本构造非参数Wasserstein任务嵌入，以估计任务相似度，再用归一化稀疏权重周期性选择并加权策略，形成新任务学习的先验。在CT-graph和MiniGrid上，作者报告其平均表现和前向迁移高于所评估的模块组合基线，且没有遗忘。Continual World结果显示，识别相关知识及确定分层组合可能需要额外调优；消融实验指出，来源选择及复用强度均与收益相关。

items.title: How to Find and Reuse Policies for Continuous Adaptation in Lifelong Reinforcement Learning

sections.text:
Finding an optimal behaviour policy within a given environment is a widely studied problem in domains as diverse as games, robotics, energy infrastructure, communication networks, and multi-agent systems.

Numerous benchmarks have been developed to support such research, but the vast majority assume that the agent's embodiment (design) is fixed, focusing instead on policy learning alone. Lifting this assumption gives rise to a broader class of problems in which optimizing embodiment and policy separately is highly suboptimal.

An agent's embodiment strongly shapes which control policies can be discovered, while the optimal embodiment is in turn defined by the policies it admits. To help the research community study this class of problems explicitly and systematically, we introduce Co-Design Gym - a suite of benchmark environments for jointly optimizing embodiment and policy.

Our environments span domains such as robotic manipulation and locomotion, multi-robot cooperation, deformable and soft dynamics, video games, electricity grids, wireless networks, F1 racing, multi-agent warehouses, and optimal control, offering 20 environment families (domains), with over 85 distinct co-design presets in total.

We further contribute a systematic evaluation of representative co-design algorithms, characterizing the current state of the art. Together, these contributions lay the groundwork for cumulative, comparable progress in co-design.

summary.en: Co-Design Gym is a benchmark suite for jointly optimizing agent embodiment and policy, addressing settings where most benchmarks fix the design and focus only on policy learning. The authors argue that embodiment shapes which control policies can be discovered, while desirable embodiment depends on the policies it enables. The suite covers domains including robotic manipulation and locomotion, multi-robot cooperation, deformable dynamics, games, electricity grids, wireless networks, F1 racing, multi-agent warehouses, and optimal control. It contains 20 environment families and more than 85 co-design presets, alongside a systematic evaluation of representative algorithms.
summary.zh: Co-Design Gym是一套用于联合优化智能体形态与策略的基准环境，针对现有多数基准将形态固定、仅关注策略学习的设定。该项目指出，形态会影响可发现的控制策略，而理想形态也取决于其支持的策略。基准覆盖机器人操作与运动、多机器人协作、可变形和软体动力学、电子游戏、电网、无线网络、F1赛车、多智能体仓库及最优控制等领域，共含20类环境和85个以上的协同设计预设。作者还系统评估了代表性算法，以支持后续可比较研究。

items.title: Co-design Gym: A Unified Benchmark for Embodiment-Policy Co-optimization

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models have scaled rapidly to enhance manipulation performance and generalizability, but this scaling incurs high computational costs that render real-world deployment increasingly challenging.

Existing approaches typically mitigate this issue by designing smaller architectures or reducing the iterative denoising steps in flow-based policies. In this work, we propose FastOPD, a foundation-to-lightweight VLA framework that enables the practical deployment of large-scale VLAs through efficient on-policy distillation.

Specifically, FastOPD adapts a flow map for single-state teacher supervision and combines it with a self-consistency objective to construct a compact student that learns the teacher dynamics.

Furthermore, we theoretically demonstrate that minimizing this objective allows the distilled student to recover a distribution on par with that induced by an ideal few-step teacher model. We evaluate FastOPD across diverse foundation policies in simulation and real-world experiments.

On LIBERO, FastOPD retains 84% of the performance of $\pi_{0.5}$ with only two inference steps, reducing inference latency by 78.1% while outperforming existing few-step distillation baselines in average success rate. With LingBot-VLA as the teacher, FastOPD improves the single-step success rate over the base student by 15.9 percentage points on RoboTwin 2.0.

We further demonstrate its applicability to a World Action Model (WAM) and deploy a compact student distilled from MolmoAct2 on a real robot.

summary.en: The paper presents FastOPD, a framework for distilling large vision-language-action models into lightweight students through efficient on-policy learning. It combines single-state teacher supervision via a flow map with a self-consistency objective; the authors theoretically claim this can recover a distribution comparable to that of an ideal few-step teacher. In simulation and real-world evaluations, a two-step student retains 84% of π0.5 performance on LIBERO while reducing latency by 78.1%. With LingBot-VLA as teacher, single-step success on RoboTwin 2.0 rises by 15.9 percentage points over the base student. The authors also report WAM applicability and deployment of a MolmoAct2-distilled student on a real robot.
summary.zh: 论文提出 FastOPD，一种通过高效在线策略蒸馏将大型视觉语言动作模型转为轻量学生模型的框架。方法结合单状态教师监督的流映射与自一致性目标；作者称其理论上可使学生恢复接近理想少步教师模型的分布。仿真和真实世界评估中，LIBERO 上学生仅用两步推理保留 π0.5 的 84% 性能、延迟降低 78.1%；以 LingBot-VLA 为教师时，RoboTwin 2.0 单步成功率较基础学生提高 15.9 个百分点。作者还报告了 WAM 应用及在真实机器人上的 MolmoAct2 蒸馏学生部署。

items.title: FastOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Lightweight VLA Deployment

sections.text:
Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) increasingly perform material transport in production logistics, where their operation is governed by job generation, dispatching and robot control. We present MoRoOp, a dataset of AMR operations recorded in a laboratory kit preparation and supply scenario over nine eight-hour shifts.

During each shift, an AMR executed stochastically generated kit supply, empty-box refill and charging jobs.

The dataset links job specifications, the operations constituting each job, dispatch events documenting operation state transitions and outcomes, and robot-state observations comprising position, orientation, velocity, per-wheel state of charge and diagnostics.

It contains 1,382 jobs, 4,815 operations, 19,352 dispatch events and 140,386 robot-state observations together with the kit specifications used during job generation. The dataset was recorded in an operating laboratory environment, and technically valid observations of delays, obstructed navigation and unsuccessful operations were retained.

Both raw and cleaned robot-state tables are provided. Documented reuse directions include the evaluation of AI agents on operational decision records, disturbance detection, operation prediction, data-driven simulation and event-log analysis.

summary.en: MoRoOp is a dataset of autonomous mobile robot operations in a laboratory kit preparation and supply scenario, recorded across nine eight-hour shifts. The robot performs stochastically generated kit supply, empty-box refill, and charging jobs. The dataset links job specifications and constituent operations with dispatch events recording state transitions and outcomes, as well as robot-state observations covering position, orientation, velocity, per-wheel charge, and diagnostics. Technically valid delays, obstructed navigation, and unsuccessful operations are retained, and both raw and cleaned state tables are provided. Suggested reuse includes evaluating decision agents, detecting disturbances, predicting operations, data-driven simulation, and event-log analysis.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 MoRoOp 数据集，记录实验室套件准备与供应场景中自主移动机器人的运行情况，覆盖九个八小时班次。机器人执行随机生成的套件供应、空箱补充和充电任务。数据关联任务规格、组成操作、记录状态转换与结果的调度事件，以及包含位置、朝向、速度、逐轮电量和诊断信息的机器人状态观测。数据集保留技术上有效的延迟、导航受阻和操作失败记录，并提供原始及清理后的状态表。作者列出的用途包括评估决策智能体、扰动检测、操作预测、数据驱动仿真和事件日志分析。

items.title: Autonomous mobile robot operations logistics: a dataset of jobs, dispatch events and robot states

sections.text:
Action-conditioned world models have become an important foundation for embodied prediction, planning, and synthetic data generation, but their errors under new task and scene distributions are often concentrated in localized spatiotemporal regions such as robot arms, manipulated objects, contact areas, and occluded objects.

This paper presents ConfAL-WM, a confidence-guided active learning framework for post-training embodied world models. Building upon EnerVerse-AC (EVAC), we attach a lightweight confidence probe to UNet decoder features and predict dense confidence maps in the latent space.

These maps are aggregated into task-, frame-, and patch-level scores, enabling data-budget allocation and localized training enhancement. Our pipeline trains the probe and warms up EVAC on a small target-domain subset.

EVAC-v1 then supplies task-level acquisition and optional frame/patch weighting signals; all selected-data models are initialized from the original pretrained EVAC checkpoint for retraining.

Experiments on RoboTwin2.0 at the default 40% data budget show that confidence-guided selection improves post-training quality, while dense frame and patch weighting offers complementary reconstruction and semantic gains compared with scalar reward, progress, and judge-based scoring baselines.

A quick visual overview of this work is available at https://ConfAL-WM.github.io.

summary.en: The paper introduces ConfAL-WM, a confidence-guided active learning framework for post-training action-conditioned world models. Built on EnerVerse-AC, it adds a lightweight probe to UNet decoder features to predict dense latent-space confidence maps, which are aggregated into task-, frame-, and patch-level scores for data allocation and localized training. The pipeline trains the probe and warms up EVAC on a small target-domain subset, then uses EVAC-v1 for task-level acquisition and optional frame or patch weighting. Experiments on RoboTwin2.0 at the default 40% data budget report improved post-training quality from confidence-guided selection, with dense weighting providing complementary reconstruction and semantic gains over several scoring baselines.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ConfAL-WM，用于动作条件世界模型后训练的置信度引导主动学习框架。该方法基于 EnerVerse-AC，在 UNet 解码器特征上增加轻量置信度探针，预测潜空间稠密置信图，并汇总为任务、帧和图块级分数，以分配数据预算和指导局部训练增强。流程先用少量目标域数据训练探针并预热 EVAC，再由 EVAC-v1 提供任务级采集及可选的帧、图块加权信号。RoboTwin2.0 默认 40% 数据预算实验显示，置信度选样提升后训练质量，稠密加权相较多种评分基线带来互补的重建与语义收益。

items.title: ConfAL-WM: Confidence-Guided Active Learning for Action-Conditioned World Models

While recent Vision-Language-Action models excel at short-horizon tasks, they lack the hierarchical reasoning required for multi-stage objectives. Furthermore, existing hierarchical agents suffer from rigid sub-task mapping, inflexible replanning, and a lack of continuous learning. To address these limitations, we introduce MobiAgent, a dual-loop agentic framework that bridges robust deployment execution and recursive policy self-improvement

sections.text:
Long-horizon mobile manipulation presents significant challenges due to compounding execution errors and capacity interference between locomotion and arm control. While recent Vision-Language-Action models excel at short-horizon tasks, they lack the hierarchical reasoning required for multi-stage objectives.

Furthermore, existing hierarchical agents suffer from rigid sub-task mapping, inflexible replanning, and a lack of continuous learning. To address these limitations, we introduce MobiAgent, a dual-loop agentic framework that bridges robust deployment execution and recursive policy self-improvement.

During deployment, the Inner Loop decouples high-level reasoning from low-level control through highly composable atomic skills. It employs Vision-Language models for receding-horizon planning and visual reflection, dynamically composing skills to ensure robust error recovery.

These skills are executed by specialized flow-matching experts that share a unified VLM backbone, maximizing reusability while mitigating capacity interference.

Concurrently, the Outer Loop drives automated lifelong learning by autonomously segmenting and verifying deployment rollouts, clustering them to discover atomic skills, and continuously fine-tuning the skill library without human annotations. Evaluations on RoboCasa, BEHAVIOR-1K, and real-world tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of MobiAgent.

It outperforms $\pi_{0.5}$-TA by 22.5 percentage points on BEHAVIOR-1K and enables robust recovery from execution failures. Through autonomous data recycling, success improves from 7.50% to 27.50% on RoboCasa and from 32.5% to 57.5% on Astribot S1.

summary.en: The paper presents MobiAgent, a dual-loop framework for long-horizon mobile manipulation that addresses compounding execution errors and capacity interference between locomotion and arm control. Its deployment loop separates high-level reasoning from low-level control using composable atomic skills, with vision-language models for receding-horizon planning and visual reflection; specialized flow-matching experts share a VLM backbone. The outer loop segments, verifies, and clusters rollouts to discover skills and continually fine-tune the skill library without human annotations. Evaluations on RoboCasa, BEHAVIOR-1K, and real-world tasks report gains over a baseline and improved success through autonomous data recycling.
summary.zh: 论文提出 MobiAgent，用于长时程移动操作的双循环智能体框架，目标是应对执行误差累积及移动与机械臂控制间的容量干扰。部署内循环通过可组合原子技能，将高层推理与低层控制分离，并用视觉语言模型进行滚动规划和视觉反思，以动态组合技能并恢复执行错误；专门的流匹配专家共享统一视觉语言模型骨干。外循环自动分段、验证和聚类部署轨迹，发现技能并持续微调技能库，无需人工标注。作者报告其在 RoboCasa、BEHAVIOR-1K 和真实任务上的评估结果，包括相对基线提升及数据循环带来的成功率改善。

items.title: MobiAgent: Dual-Loop Recursive Policy Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation

End-to-end vision-language-action policies provide strong manipulation capabilities, but their transfer to physical environments typically relies on calibrating simulated visual and dynamical conditions, collecting additional target-domain demonstrations, and optimizing the policy through further training. sections.text:
A key challenge in bringing embodied intelligence into the real world is transferring capabilities from simulation to reality and enabling agents to continually adapt after deployment.

End-to-end vision-language-action policies provide strong manipulation capabilities, but their transfer to physical environments typically relies on calibrating simulated visual and dynamical conditions, collecting additional target-domain demonstrations, and optimizing the policy through further training.

Tool-using embodied agents offer flexible task orchestration, yet existing systems primarily emphasize task execution and experience reuse within a given environment, with limited support for transferring procedural knowledge and continuously adapting it across simulation and reality.

We propose RoboBridge, a framework that treats sim-to-real transfer as the continued adaptation of executable task skills. The agent represents task knowledge as procedures connecting task intent, observations, tool operations, and outcome verification.

Interaction feedback is used to generate candidate skill revisions, which are evaluated before being persisted or rejected. A pretrained vision-language-action policy is exposed as a reusable action tool and enhanced with inference-time guidance, enabling fine-grained execution without retraining the underlying policy.

RoboBridge grounds transferable skills in task semantics and interaction interfaces shared across simulation and reality. This representation preserves reusable task structure while allowing environment-dependent operations to be selectively revised through real-world execution feedback.

We evaluate the framework on LIBERO-PRO and corresponding physical tasks, studying both skill evolution and post-transfer adaptation. Our framework provides a route from one-shot policy deployment to continual procedural learning across environments.

summary.en: The paper proposes RoboBridge, a framework for sim-to-real transfer that represents task knowledge as executable procedures linking intent, observations, tool operations, and outcome verification. Interaction feedback generates candidate skill revisions, which are evaluated before acceptance or rejection. A pretrained vision-language-action policy serves as a reusable action tool with inference-time guidance, without retraining the underlying policy. The authors evaluate skill evolution and post-transfer adaptation on LIBERO-PRO and corresponding physical tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出 RoboBridge，一个面向具身智能仿真到现实迁移的框架，将任务知识表示为连接任务意图、观察、工具操作和结果验证的可执行流程。框架利用交互反馈提出技能修订并评估后再保留或拒绝，将预训练视觉—语言—动作策略作为可复用动作工具，通过推理时引导实现细粒度执行而无需重新训练底层策略。作者在 LIBERO-PRO 及对应实体任务上评估技能演化和迁移后的适应。

items.title: RoboBridge: A Self-Evolving Embodied Agent Framework for Sim-to-Real Transfer

The objective was to develop a responsive and intuitive assistive device that adapts to various object shapes while providing sensory feedback to the user. The system relies on EMG signals to control the motion of a flexible, biomimetic structure whose curling geometry follows a logarithmic spiral, enabling it to coil around

sections.text:
This paper presents the design and evaluation of a myoelectric tentacle-shaped prosthesis integrating electromyographic (EMG) control, sensorless object detection, and vibrotactile feedback. The objective was to develop a responsive and intuitive assistive device that adapts to various object shapes while providing sensory feedback to the user.

The system relies on EMG signals to control the motion of a flexible, biomimetic structure whose curling geometry follows a logarithmic spiral, enabling it to coil around objects. To ensure stable control, the EMG signal is normalized and filtered, and a threshold-based method identifies user intention.

Object contact is detected through a slope-based analysis of motor current, eliminating the need for external sensors, and a haptic feedback strategy based on cumulative vibrotactile stimulation conveys spatial information about the tentacle's configuration. The system was evaluated through quantitative and qualitative tests.

The results demonstrate a low response time (77 ms on average), enabling smooth real-time interaction; an object-detection success rate above 90%, confirming robustness despite EMG variability; and an effective haptic feedback strategy that allowed users to reliably identify the folding zone of the tentacle.

The proposed biomimetic design promotes further investigation of expressive artificial limbs by prioritizing expressive functionality over adherence to a predefined, anthropomorphic form factor.

summary.en: This paper presents and evaluates a biomimetic tentacle-shaped myoelectric prosthesis combining EMG control, sensorless object-contact detection, and vibrotactile feedback. Its flexible structure curls around objects following a logarithmic spiral. The system filters and normalizes EMG signals, uses a threshold to identify user intent, and detects contact by analyzing motor-current slopes. Quantitative and qualitative tests report an average response time of 77 ms, object-detection success above 90%, and users' reliable identification of the tentacle's folding zone.
summary.zh: 论文介绍并评估一种仿生触手形肌电假肢，结合肌电控制、无外部传感器的物体接触检测和振动触觉反馈。柔性结构按对数螺旋形态卷绕物体；系统通过滤波、归一化肌电信号及阈值识别用户意图，并根据电机电流斜率检测接触。定量与定性测试显示，平均响应时间为77毫秒，物体检测成功率超过90%，用户能够可靠识别触手的折叠区域。

items.title: A Biomimetic Myoelectric Tentacle Prosthesis with Sensorless Object Detection and Vibrotactile Feedback

items.intro: arXiv:2610.02339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robot demonstrations may contain useful behavior even when individual episodes are inefficient or unsuccessful. Trajectory stitching offers a way to compose these behaviors into improved training data, but identifying useful connections and verifying their feasibility is difficult in high-dimensional robot data, where many prior methods rely on low-dimensional state representations. We introduce NEEDLE, an offline dataset-augmentation algorithm that addresses these challenges by adding short, verified action bridges between recorded observations in high-dimensional robot

sections.text:
Robot demonstrations may contain useful behavior even when individual episodes are inefficient or unsuccessful.

Trajectory stitching offers a way to compose these behaviors into improved training data, but identifying useful connections and verifying their feasibility is difficult in high-dimensional robot data, where many prior methods rely on low-dimensional state representations.

We introduce NEEDLE, an offline dataset-augmentation algorithm that addresses these challenges by adding short, verified action bridges between recorded observations in high-dimensional robot demonstrations.

First, NEEDLE identifies and creates connections that bypass suboptimal detours, broaden action coverage, and augment the original dataset with failed trajectories, using only RGB images, proprioception, and episode-level outcomes, without new environment interaction or privileged object state.

Next, we present a sampling technique that incorporates accepted bridges into policy training without synthesizing intermediate images or discarding the original demonstrations, allowing policies to learn alternative actions while retaining the original dataset's coverage.

On real-robot tasks, NEEDLE improves success rate over the strongest baseline on each task by an average of 21 percentage points. Videos and supplementary materials are on https://needle-work.github.io/.

summary.en: The paper introduces NEEDLE, an offline robot dataset-augmentation algorithm that adds short, verified action bridges between recorded observations in high-dimensional demonstrations. The bridges can bypass suboptimal detours and expand action coverage. NEEDLE uses only RGB images, proprioception, and episode-level outcomes, without new environment interaction or privileged object state. A sampling method incorporates accepted bridges into policy training while retaining the original demonstrations. On real-robot tasks, the reported success rate improves by an average of 21 percentage points over the strongest baseline for each task.
summary.zh: 论文提出 NEEDLE，一种离线机器人数据集增强算法，通过在高维演示数据的已记录观察之间添加经过验证的短动作桥接，绕过低效路径并扩展动作覆盖。该方法仅使用 RGB 图像、本体感知和回合级结果，无需新的环境交互或特权物体状态。其采样方法将获接受的桥接纳入策略训练，同时保留原始演示数据。在真实机器人任务中，相较各任务最强基线，成功率平均提高21个百分点。

items.title: NEEDLEWORK: Offline Rewriting of Robot Data with Verified Local Stitches

sections.text:
In dynamic open-world environments, autonomous agents often encounter novelties that hinder their ability to find plans to achieve their goals. Specifically, traditional symbolic planners fail to generate plans when the robot's planning domain lacks the operators that enable it to interact appropriately with novel objects in the environment.

We propose a neuro-symbolic architecture that integrates symbolic planning, reinforcement learning, and a large language model (LLM) to learn how to handle novel objects.

In particular, we leverage the common sense reasoning capability of the LLM to identify missing operators, generate plans with the symbolic AI planner, and write reward functions to guide the reinforcement learning agent in learning control policies for newly identified operators.

Our method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in operator discovery as well as operator learning in continuous robotic domains.Our webpage and code can be access here: https://helenlu66.github.io/hybridLLMguided/

summary.en: The paper proposes a neuro-symbolic architecture combining symbolic planning, reinforcement learning, and a large language model to help agents handle novel objects in open-world environments. When a planning domain lacks operators needed to interact with such objects, the LLM uses common-sense reasoning to identify missing operators and writes reward functions to guide reinforcement learning in learning their control policies. A symbolic planner generates plans. The authors report that their method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in operator discovery and learning in continuous robotic domains.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种结合符号规划、强化学习与大型语言模型的神经符号架构，用于帮助自主智能体应对开放环境中的新颖物体。当规划领域缺少与新物体交互所需的操作符时，语言模型利用常识推理识别缺失操作符，并为强化学习智能体编写奖励函数，以学习相应控制策略；符号规划器则生成计划。作者称，该方法在连续机器人领域的操作符发现和学习方面均优于现有先进方法。

items.title: Novelty Adaptation Through Hybrid Large Language Model (LLM)-Symbolic Planning and LLM-guided Reinforcement Learning

sections.text:
Long-horizon tasks with sparse rewards pose an exploration bottleneck for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning: a policy started from the initial state rarely reaches the goal and receives no learning signal.

Reference motions, hand-designed curricula, and shaped rewards supply this signal but require demonstrations or task-specific engineering; automatic start-state and goal curricula avoid this but typically expand from one side only, so the full distance to the target must be covered from that side.

We propose the Bidirectional Voronoi-biased Exploration curriculum for Reinforcement learning (BVER), which expands from both ends at once.

Inspired by bidirectional RRT planning, BVER grows start states outward from the goal and goals outward from the initial state distribution, biases both toward unexplored task space, and steers them toward each other, training one goal-conditioned policy on both.

On point-mass mazes, quadrupedal box climbing, and robot-arm ring-on-peg transfer, BVER learns faster than all compared reference-free curricula.

On box climbing, it reaches 95% success on a 0.4 m box in roughly 65% fewer iterations than the best of them, is the only one of them to learn to climb a 0.7 m box, and yields a policy robust to start, goal, and yaw variation.

Without a demonstration, it approaches the sample efficiency of reference-based curricula on the 0.4 m box and on ring-on-peg transfer. Ablations show that expanding from both ends outperforms either direction alone.

summary.en: The paper introduces BVER, a bidirectional exploration curriculum for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning. It expands start states from the goal and goals from the initial-state distribution, biases both toward unexplored task space, and steers them toward each other while training one policy. Across point-mass mazes, quadrupedal box climbing, and robot-arm ring transfer, the authors report faster learning than the compared reference-free curricula. Ablations indicate that bidirectional expansion outperforms either direction alone.
summary.zh: 论文提出面向目标条件强化学习的双向 Voronoi 偏置探索课程 BVER，同时从目标向外扩展起始状态、从初始状态分布向外扩展目标，并引导两侧探索相遇，以训练单一策略。在点质量迷宫、四足机器人爬箱和机械臂套环任务中，作者报告其学习速度超过所比较的免参考课程；爬箱仿真中，达到指定箱体成功率所需迭代更少，并能学会攀爬更高箱体。消融结果显示双向扩展优于单向扩展。

items.title: Bidirectional Voronoi-biased Exploration Curriculum for Reinforcement Learning

We introduce DriftWorld, an action-conditioned world model based on drifting generative models. DriftWorld learns a conditional drift during training, enabling it to generate future observations for a given action sequence in a single forward pass during inference. Across Bridge-V2, RT-1, Language Table, Push-T, and Robomimic, DriftWorld

sections.text:
Predictive world models enable robots to simulate the visual outcomes of their actions, but state-of-the-art diffusion-based models remain costly because generating each rollout requires multi-step iterative denoising. We introduce DriftWorld, an action-conditioned world model based on drifting generative models.

DriftWorld learns a conditional drift during training, enabling it to generate future observations for a given action sequence in a single forward pass during inference.

Across Bridge-V2, RT-1, Language Table, Push-T, and Robomimic, DriftWorld runs at over 40 fps and is 12+ times faster than diffusion-based baselines, while matching or improving their visual generation quality.

This makes DriftWorld an efficient world model for robot simulation and further enables downstream applications including inference-time action search and offline policy evaluation.

summary.en: DriftWorld is an action-conditioned world model based on drifting generative models. It learns a conditional drift during training and generates future observations for an action sequence in a single forward pass at inference. On Bridge-V2, RT-1, Language Table, Push-T, and Robomimic, the authors report speeds above 40 frames per second and at least 12 times faster inference than diffusion-based baselines, with comparable or improved visual generation quality. They also describe applications in action search and offline policy evaluation.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DriftWorld，一种基于漂移生成模型的动作条件世界模型。模型在训练时学习条件漂移，使其在推理时能够通过一次前向计算，根据动作序列生成未来观测。作者在 Bridge-V2、RT-1、Language Table、Push-T 和 Robomimic 上报告，该模型运行速度超过每秒 40 帧，比扩散模型基线快至少 12 倍，同时视觉生成质量相当或更好。论文还指出，这种效率支持推理时动作搜索和离线策略评估等应用。

items.title: DriftWorld: Fast World Modeling through Drifting

Using these assets, a solver-based assessment computes grasp-specific damage thresholds from object geometry, material properties, and recorded grasp conditions and compares them with recorded contact forces to assess potential deformation and fracture. sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models aim to perform diverse manipulation tasks, but task success in existing rigid-body benchmarks does not indicate whether they preserve objects. We introduce ManiPhysicsZoo, which consolidates literature-supported material properties, 3D meshes, and supporting references into reusable object assets.

Using these assets, a solver-based assessment computes grasp-specific damage thresholds from object geometry, material properties, and recorded grasp conditions and compares them with recorded contact forces to assess potential deformation and fracture.

Building on these components, ManiPhysicsBench evaluates object preservation in LIBERO and SimplerEnv across three physics axes and three difficulty levels. Public VLA checkpoints show a substantial gap between task success and safe success, defined as task completion while preserving the object.

Their gripper commands concentrate near full opening and closure, with largely similar aggregate distributions across objects, consistent with binary gripper supervision. We examine how object-specific continuous gripper labels change model behavior by retraining a VLA model.

The retrained model shows more object-dependent gripping and higher safe success, but lower task success and limited generalization of object-preserving behavior.

summary.en: The paper presents ManiPhysicsZoo, a collection of object assets, and ManiPhysicsBench for evaluating whether vision-language-action models preserve objects during manipulation. A solver estimates damage thresholds from geometry, material properties, and grasp conditions, then compares them with recorded contact forces to assess possible deformation or fracture. Evaluations in LIBERO and SimplerEnv reveal a gap between task success and safe success. Retraining with object-specific continuous gripper labels produces more object-dependent gripping and higher safe success, but lower task success and limited generalization of preservation behavior.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 ManiPhysicsZoo 对象资产库，并据此构建 ManiPhysicsBench，用于评估视觉语言动作模型在操作任务中是否保持物体完好。基于物体几何、材料属性和抓取条件，求解器计算损伤阈值，并与记录的接触力比较，以评估潜在变形或断裂。对 LIBERO 和 SimplerEnv 的评估显示，任务成功与安全成功之间存在明显差距。作者还发现，使用对象特定的连续夹爪标签重新训练后，抓取行为更依对象而变且安全成功率更高，但任务成功率较低，保物行为的泛化有限。

items.title: ManiPhysicsBench: Physics-Based Assessment of Object Preservation in VLA Manipulation

Whether this paradigm is also safe, however, has not been asked. We evaluate coding agents under a safety constraint, where each task pairs a manipulation goal with an obstacle the robot must not touch. The agent pursues the goal but

sections.text:
Coding agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot manipulation: a language model writes the robot controller as a program, and agents built in this way now operate robots without robot-specific training. Whether this paradigm is also safe, however, has not been asked.

We evaluate coding agents under a safety constraint, where each task pairs a manipulation goal with an obstacle the robot must not touch. The agent pursues the goal but collides with the obstacle in most cases, treating task completion as its sole objective.

The agent reasons about the obstacle in its traces, and the prompt already forbids touching it, so neither perception nor instruction is at fault; the fault lies in the planning, where the stated constraint never becomes a priority. By decomposing manipulation into a route phase and a contact-rich moment, we locate the source of the failure.

Along the route, the model cannot prioritize the safety constraint, having no notion of a clearing route and none of replanning once a chosen route becomes infeasible. At the contact, it is unaware that contact execution is bounded by the same constraint. To close this gap, we present SafeHarness, which equips the model with two obstacle-aware harnesses.

Obstacle-aware route planning grounds the objects as bounding boxes and draws candidate routes over them as sequences of waypoints. The agent then plans a route in advance, verifies it, replans when necessary, and only then executes it. Obstacle-aware contact execution instead selects the contact position so that the contact itself avoids the obstacle.

SafeHarness attains 81.2% task success and 91.9% collision avoidance with GPT-6-Astra, surpassing the previous SOTA by 13.7 and 23.0 points, and the same agent without harnesses by 31.2 and 57.5 points, respectively.

summary.en: The paper evaluates coding agents on robot manipulation tasks that require achieving a goal while avoiding an obstacle. The agent collides in most cases, despite reasoning about the obstacle and receiving an instruction not to touch it. The authors attribute the failures to planning, including weak prioritization of safety, lack of route checking and replanning, and failure to apply the constraint during contact. SafeHarness adds obstacle-aware waypoint route planning, verification and replanning, plus contact-position selection that avoids obstacles. With GPT-6-Astra, the authors report 81.2% task success and 91.9% collision avoidance.
summary.zh: 论文评估编程智能体执行机器人操作时的安全性：任务要求机器人达成操作目标，同时避开障碍物。作者报告，智能体虽能在推理记录中识别障碍物且提示已禁止碰撞，仍在多数案例中发生碰撞。分析将问题定位于规划：智能体未优先处理安全约束，也缺少路线清空判断、重规划能力及对接触阶段约束的认识。为此提出 SafeHarness，加入基于边界框和航点的障碍感知路线规划与验证、必要时重规划，以及避障接触位置选择。使用 GPT-6-Astra 时，论文报告任务成功率为 81.2%，避碰率为 91.9%。

items.title: Coding Agents with Harness for Safe Robot Control

items.intro: arXiv:2606.01332v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of scaling dynamic loco-manipulation from a single free-rolling sphere to multiple spheres transported simultaneously on the back of a wheel-legged quadruped, without fences, grippers, or mechanical stops. Multiple identical free-rolling spheres form an unordered set with no persistent identity: their ordering may change independently at each history frame, creating a \emph{per-frame permutation symmetry} that standard history-concatenation set encoders do not explicitly enforce -- these encoders impose only a shared

sections.text:
We study the problem of scaling dynamic loco-manipulation from a single free-rolling sphere to multiple spheres transported simultaneously on the back of a wheel-legged quadruped, without fences, grippers, or mechanical stops.

Multiple identical free-rolling spheres form an unordered set with no persistent identity: their ordering may change independently at each history frame, creating a \emph{per-frame permutation symmetry} that standard history-concatenation set encoders do not explicitly enforce -- these encoders impose only a shared, diagonal permutation symmetry over the full history.

We show that this symmetry mismatch leads to a concrete failure mode in curriculum-based reinforcement learning.

Within the same PPO training budget, flat MLPs and branch-wise encoders plateau at or below the two-sphere stage, while a history-concatenation Deep Sets baseline (\HCDS) fails to progress past the two-sphere stage in our runs unless ball-to-slot assignments are randomised during training, suggesting that it exploits slot indices as a curriculum shortcut rather than learning identity-free multi-sphere dynamics.

We propose \textbf{Per-Frame Deep Sets (\PFDS)}, which performs permutation-invariant pooling within each history frame before temporal readout; we prove that \PFDS is $\Gframe$-invariant and universally approximates continuous $\Gframe$-invariant policies.

A $2{\times}2$ ablation over encoder architecture and slot randomisation separates the architectural and data-augmentation pathways, and \PFDS reaches the five-sphere stage with 100\% no-drop transport in simulation across all five random seeds.

We further distill the \PFDS teacher into \TactSet via DAgger, replacing privileged sphere-state observations with a $16{\times}16$ Boolean union contact map, yielding a compact and naturally $\Gframe$-invariant tactile representation.

summary.en: This paper studies transporting multiple free-rolling spheres on a wheel-legged quadruped and identifies a mismatch between per-frame sphere order changes and conventional history-concatenation encoders. The authors propose Per-Frame Deep Sets (PFDS), which pools permutation-invariant features within each history frame before temporal readout. They prove its invariance and universal approximation property for continuous invariant policies. Under the reported PPO budget, PFDS reaches the five-sphere stage with no drops in simulation across five seeds. The teacher is also distilled with DAgger into a tactile representation based on a Boolean contact map.
summary.zh: 论文研究轮足四足机器人在背部同时运输多个自由滚动球体的问题，重点指出球体在每段历史中的无序性与常规历史拼接编码器的对称性不匹配。作者提出逐帧深度集合（PFDS），先在每帧内进行置换不变池化，再进行时间读取，并证明其不变性及连续不变策略的通用逼近性质。在相同 PPO 训练预算下，仿真中 PFDS 在五个随机种子上均达到五球阶段且无球掉落；作者还通过 DAgger 将其蒸馏为使用布尔接触图的触觉表示。

items.title: S2M-Trek: From Single to Multi-Sphere Transport via Per-Frame Deep Sets on a Wheel-Legged Robot

This tackles the current solutions revolving around rigid person finding systems requiring exact knowledge of the individual for item-delivery in indoor settings. While the focus in literature is on learned methods using unavailable public or sparse data due to human privacy. We propose a planning framework that combines distance and

sections.text:
We address the Person Goal Navigation (PersonNav) problem, enabling robots to search for people under realistic constraints on information accessibility and language uncertainty. This tackles the current solutions revolving around rigid person finding systems requiring exact knowledge of the individual for item-delivery in indoor settings.

While the focus in literature is on learned methods using unavailable public or sparse data due to human privacy. We propose a planning framework that combines distance and semantic information about the recipient (habits and intent) weighted by the trust of the user-provided information.

A synthetic benchmark of scenarios is also developed including actors, items, and requests to evaluate performance before real-world deployment aiming to simulate natural language human-robot interactions. Results show our informed search outperforms classical distance-based graph baselines, while semantics alone lead to ungrounded, sporadic search.

Our method achieves strong gains over baselines, with an LLM-based variant performing comparably, and its explicit belief representation naturally supports future Bayesian filtering. Hardware tests demonstrate our method supports real-world embodiment able to leverage between semantic and distance information in a real setting.

This work moves toward more intelligent mobile service agents capable of human-like, informed search in realistic environments to be leveraged in day-to-day use. https://anonymous.4open.science/r/personnavsite-4ED2/index.html.

summary.en: This paper addresses Person Goal Navigation with a planning framework that combines distance, recipient-related semantics such as habits and intent, and trust in user-provided information. The authors develop a synthetic benchmark with actors, items, and requests. They report that informed search outperforms classical distance-based graph baselines, while semantics alone produces ungrounded, sporadic search. An LLM-based variant performs comparably, and hardware tests show that the method can combine semantic and distance information in a real setting. The abstract gives no numerical effect size.
summary.zh: 论文针对个人目标导航，提出一种结合距离、收件人的语义信息（如习惯和意图）及用户信息可信度的机器人搜索规划框架，并构建包含角色、物品和请求的合成场景基准。作者报告，该方法优于经典的基于距离的图搜索基线；仅使用语义信息会导致缺乏依据且零散的搜索。基于大语言模型的变体表现相近，硬件测试则显示该方法可在真实环境中结合语义与距离信息。摘要未提供具体提升幅度。

items.title: CSIR: Contextually and Socially Informed Robots for Efficient Person Goal Navigation

How can a pretrained WAM learn from a stronger Teacher on the histories it encounters during execution? We present WAM-OPD, which collects Student rollout histories and queries a Teacher for paired video and action targets. The Student learns from both targets while retaining its one-step video and action generation at deployment. Across 12 RoboTwin 2

sections.text:
World Action Models (WAMs) generate both future video and robot actions, offering two connected outputs for post-training supervision. How can a pretrained WAM learn from a stronger Teacher on the histories it encounters during execution? We present WAM-OPD, which collects Student rollout histories and queries a Teacher for paired video and action targets.

The Student learns from both targets while retaining its one-step video and action generation at deployment. Across 12 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, WAM-OPD improves average success from 33.8% to 65.7%; across four real-robot tasks, it improves average success from 51.4% to 64.6%.

With the collected Student histories held fixed, joint video-action supervision achieves the highest observed success on all three ablation tasks, while either modality alone also improves performance. A separate comparison with Teacher-generated histories finds task-dependent differences between the two history sources.

These results demonstrate the value of paired video-action supervision for improving WAM policies without increasing their deployed sampling budget.

summary.en: The authors present WAM-OPD, a post-training method for world action models. It collects Student rollout histories and queries a Teacher for paired video and action targets, which the Student learns from jointly. Reported average success rises from 33.8% to 65.7% across 12 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and from 51.4% to 64.6% across four real-robot tasks. With Student histories fixed, joint supervision has the highest observed success on all three ablation tasks, while either modality alone also helps. Comparisons of history sources vary by task.
summary.zh: 论文提出 WAM-OPD，用于世界动作模型的后训练：收集学生模型执行时的历史，并向教师模型查询配对的视频与动作目标，供学生同时学习。作者报告，在 RoboTwin 2.0 的12项任务中，平均成功率从33.8%升至65.7%；在四项真实机器人任务中，从51.4%升至64.6%。固定学生历史的消融实验中，联合监督在三项任务上取得最高观测成功率，单一模态也能改善表现；教师生成历史与学生历史的比较则因任务而异。

items.title: WAM-OPD: Joint Video-Action Supervision for World Action Model Post-Training with On-Policy Distillation

items.intro: arXiv:2610.00330v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Long-term object search requires learning where objects usually appear from repeated but uneven observations of a changing environment. We formulate retrospective open-vocabulary memory as probabilistic inference from censored observations, where the key idea is to reason with evidence per opportunity: a detection or non-detection should influence belief only in proportion to the robot's opportunity to observe the corresponding location. We introduce ECROM, which uses this principle to estimate long-term prevalence for concepts specified

sections.text:
Long-term object search requires learning where objects usually appear from repeated but uneven observations of a changing environment.

We formulate retrospective open-vocabulary memory as probabilistic inference from censored observations, where the key idea is to reason with evidence per opportunity: a detection or non-detection should influence belief only in proportion to the robot's opportunity to observe the corresponding location.

We introduce ECROM, which uses this principle to estimate long-term prevalence for concepts specified only at query time and converts the resulting belief directly into an active-search prior.

To evaluate this problem, we introduce a controlled long-term benchmark in ten HM3D homes that independently varies object placement and observation opportunity across repeated traversals. ECROM improves support-level AP on held-out queries by 4.5 points and search SPL by 4.2 points over the strongest competing memory in each metric.

The benchmark, dataset, and code will be open-sourced. Project page: https://jiaming.im/ecrom/

summary.en: This paper formulates retrospective open-vocabulary memory for long-term object search as probabilistic inference from censored observations. Its central principle is to weight detections and non-detections according to the robot’s opportunity to observe each location. The authors introduce ECROM to estimate long-term prevalence for concepts specified at query time and use the resulting belief as an active-search prior. In a controlled benchmark across ten HM3D homes, ECROM improves support-level AP on held-out queries by 4.5 points and search SPL by 4.2 points over the strongest competing memory on each metric.
summary.zh: 论文研究长期物体搜索中的开放词汇记忆，针对环境变化且观察机会不均的问题，将其表述为基于删失观测的概率推断：检测或未检测的证据应按机器人观察相应位置的机会加权。作者提出 ECROM，用于估计查询时才指定概念的长期出现率，并将信念转化为主动搜索先验。评测基准覆盖十个 HM3D 家庭，分别控制物体放置与观察机会。作者报告，ECROM 在留出查询上的支持级 AP 提高4.5点，搜索 SPL 提高4.2点。

items.title: Retrospective Open-Vocabulary Memory for Long-Term Object Search

items.intro: arXiv:2610.03710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by human vision, we introduce a framework using active gaze to enable fine-grained bimanual manipulation with only a single stereo camera. EyeRobot 2.0 physically attends to a 3D fixation point in the scene by swiveling two eye viewpoints to center their gaze on it. The resulting images are processed foveally by allocating more visual tokens to the image centers, focusing computation on task-relevant features. Such Active Visual Fixation (AVF) requires carefully

sections.text:
Inspired by human vision, we introduce a framework using active gaze to enable fine-grained bimanual manipulation with only a single stereo camera. EyeRobot 2.0 physically attends to a 3D fixation point in the scene by swiveling two eye viewpoints to center their gaze on it.

The resulting images are processed foveally by allocating more visual tokens to the image centers, focusing computation on task-relevant features.

Such Active Visual Fixation (AVF) requires carefully coordinated gaze during task execution, which we accomplish hierarchically by first training a low-level gaze servoing policy conditioned on a goal object, then training a target selector which emits fixation goals based on task progress.

Both modules are trained with RL on real-world data: the first is trained with a dense geometric reward and the second co-trains with the BC gripper policy which allows it to discover fixation sequences that can resemble a human's fixation sequence while performing the task.

EyeRobot 2.0 further takes advantage of fixation by canonicalizing gripper information into a fixation-relative SE（3） frame, which compacts the size of the action distribution to learn.

We collect teleoperation data for 7 real-world and 6 simulated tasks, and conduct over 1000 physical and 1800 simulated robot trials comparing EyeRobot 2.0 against passive stereo and ego + wrist camera policies trained on the same data. Removing wrist cameras is costly for standard policies: with only passive stereo, real-world success drops from 52% to 27%.

EyeRobot 2.0 closes this gap with only stereo, outperforming passive stereo by 40% in real and 20% in sim. It matches ego + wrist policies when their wrist views are clear (69% vs. 64%), and more than doubles their success when grasped objects occlude the wrist cameras (48% vs. 22%)

summary.en: The paper introduces EyeRobot 2.0, which actively steers two eye viewpoints toward 3D fixation points and gives image centers more visual tokens to support bimanual manipulation with one stereo camera. It hierarchically trains gaze servoing and fixation-goal selection, and represents gripper information relative to the fixation frame. In reported real and simulated trials, passive stereo policies lose performance without wrist cameras. EyeRobot 2.0 improves over passive stereo and performs especially well when grasped objects occlude wrist-camera views.
summary.zh: 论文提出 EyeRobot 2.0，利用双眼视角主动转向场景中的三维注视点，并对图像中心分配更多视觉令牌，以单个立体相机支持双臂精细操作。系统分层训练注视控制和目标选择策略，并将夹爪信息表示在相对注视点的坐标系中。作者报告了真实与模拟任务试验：仅用被动立体视觉的标准策略真实成功率由52%降至27%；EyeRobot 2.0较被动立体视觉在真实和模拟中分别高40%和20%，并在腕部视野被遮挡时优于带腕部相机策略。

items.title: EyeRobot 2.0: Active Gaze for Precise Manipulation without Wrist Cameras

Our implementation has modular dynamics and integrators, and we validate it on the F1TENTH platform under constrained computation and noisy state estimation. The system identifies tire parameters online by evaluating thousands of

sections.text:
We present a generalized implementation of Look-Back and Look-Ahead Adaptive Model Predictive Control (LLA-MPC), a learning-free framework for real-time, rapid adaptive system identification and control. The original formulation was demonstrated only in simulation, for autonomous racing with a fixed model structure.

Our implementation has modular dynamics and integrators, and we validate it on the F1TENTH platform under constrained computation and noisy state estimation. The system identifies tire parameters online by evaluating thousands of candidate models in real time on an embedded computer.

Experiments with low-friction tires across changing surfaces show that LLA-MPC completes high-speed tracking tasks where a fixed nominal model fails. Code, videos, and our related work are available at: https://lla-control.github.io.

summary.en: The paper presents a generalized implementation of Look-Back and Look-Ahead Adaptive Model Predictive Control, a learning-free framework for rapid online system identification and control. Its modular dynamics and integrators are validated on the F1TENTH platform under limited computation and noisy state estimates. The system evaluates thousands of candidate models on embedded hardware to identify tire parameters online. Experiments with low-friction tires across changing surfaces report successful high-speed tracking where a fixed nominal model fails.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 Look-Back and Look-Ahead Adaptive Model Predictive Control（LLA-MPC）的通用实现。这一无需学习的框架通过实时评估大量候选模型进行系统辨识与控制；实现包含模块化动力学和积分器。作者在计算受限、状态估计含噪的 F1TENTH 平台上验证系统，在线辨识轮胎参数。低摩擦轮胎在不同路面上的实验显示，该方法能完成高速跟踪任务，而固定标称模型会失败。

items.title: LLA-MPC on Embedded Hardware: Rapid Adaptive Control with Thousands of Parallel Models

sections.text:
Long-horizon compositional manipulation has become increasingly important for real-world robot deployment, where a single task involves multiple coordinated subtasks. Existing world-action models (WAMs) jointly predict short-horizon visual futures and actions, but typically lack explicit subtask-level reasoning.

We propose Visual Goal-conditioned Action Reasoning (ViGAR), a hierarchical framework that factorizes manipulation into a visual subgoal planner and a subgoal executor. Given the current observation and global instruction, the subgoal planner predicts a visual subgoal for the next subtask.

The subgoal executor then jointly generates future visual trajectories and actions conditioned on the predicted subgoal. Both components share a pretrained world-model representation, enabling task-level planning and action generation to benefit from common physical knowledge.

Moreover, our framework naturally supports in-context learning: using a global goal image as context can induce different subtask decompositions and behaviors without parameter updates.

On the RoboTwin Clean2Random benchmark, ViGAR achieves 82.00% and 67.02% success rates under the Clean and Random settings, respectively, surpassing the strongest baseline by 12.86 percentage points in average success rate. Real-world robot experiments on five compositional and two in-context learning tasks further confirm the effectiveness of ViGAR.

summary.en: The paper proposes ViGAR, a hierarchical framework for long-horizon compositional manipulation. A visual subgoal planner predicts the next subtask's visual goal from the observation and global instruction; an executor then generates future visual trajectories and actions conditioned on that goal. Both components share a pretrained world-model representation. The framework also supports in-context behavior changes using a global goal image without parameter updates. On RoboTwin Clean2Random, reported success rates are 82.00% in Clean and 67.02% in Random; real-robot experiments cover compositional and in-context tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ViGAR，将长时程组合操作拆分为视觉子目标规划器和子目标执行器：前者根据当前观察和全局指令预测下一子任务的视觉目标，后者据此联合生成未来视觉轨迹与动作。两部分共享预训练世界模型表示，并支持通过全局目标图像进行无需参数更新的情境学习。在 RoboTwin Clean2Random 基准的 Clean 和 Random 设置中，成功率分别为82.00%和67.02%；作者还报告了五项组合任务和两项情境学习任务的真实机器人实验。

items.title: Rethinking World-Action Model for Compositional and In-Context Robotic Manipulation

items.intro: arXiv:2610.02874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalable driving simulators typically execute vehicle commands using prescribed behavioral or kinematic rules, overlooking the physics of tire-road interfaces, thereby limiting their ability to capture how adverse road and environmental conditions alter vehicle execution and propagate through traffic. To address this limitation, we present SceneFactory-3D, a GPU-batched, physics-grounded multi-agent driving simulator. Vehicles execute acceleration and steering commands via suspension- and friction-limited forces evaluated at each wheel-contact point. Spatially varying friction, per-world 3D heightfields

sections.text:
Scalable driving simulators typically execute vehicle commands using prescribed behavioral or kinematic rules, overlooking the physics of tire-road interfaces, thereby limiting their ability to capture how adverse road and environmental conditions alter vehicle execution and propagate through traffic.

To address this limitation, we present SceneFactory-3D, a GPU-batched, physics-grounded multi-agent driving simulator. Vehicles execute acceleration and steering commands via suspension- and friction-limited forces evaluated at each wheel-contact point.

Spatially varying friction, per-world 3D heightfields, gravity, and rigid contact consistently govern wheel motion and chassis collisions.

Per-world terrain isolation and GPU batching enable SceneFactory-3D to run matched physical counterfactuals in parallel: traffic scenario setup and vehicle controllers remain fixed while only the road condition changes, enabling the resulting closed-loop effects to be evaluated across parallel worlds.

To demonstrate the advantage of the SceneFactory-3D-enabled counterfactual evaluation, we conduct an empirical study on vehicle controllers' sensitivity to road conditions. We study three learned-policy families on 1,024 matched 12-vehicle worlds per condition, and two classical planners on a shared 32-world subset, across 21 friction and grade conditions.

When friction drops from 1.0 to 0.18, the share of vehicles that clear the work zone safely falls by 6 to 90 percentage points across learned policies (18-19 for classical planners), and near-collision situations become more frequent for every learned policy. Code: https://github.com/SmallWorldLab/SceneFactory_3D

summary.en: The paper presents SceneFactory-3D, a GPU-batched, physics-grounded multi-agent driving simulator. Vehicle commands are executed through suspension- and friction-limited forces at wheel contacts, with varying friction, 3D terrain, gravity, and rigid contacts represented. Its counterfactual evaluation keeps scenario setup and controllers fixed while changing road conditions across parallel worlds. In the reported study, reducing friction from 1.0 to 0.18 lowered safe work-zone clearance among learned policies by 6 to 90 percentage points and among classical planners by 18 to 19 points; near collisions became more frequent for every learned policy.
summary.zh: 论文提出 SceneFactory-3D，一种 GPU 批处理、基于物理的多智能体驾驶模拟器，以轮胎接地点的悬架和摩擦限制力执行车辆指令，并通过摩擦变化、三维地形、重力和刚体接触模拟路面条件。其反事实评估在并行世界中固定交通场景和控制器、只改变路况。作者研究了不同摩擦和坡度条件下学习策略与经典规划器的表现；摩擦系数从1.0降至0.18时，学习策略安全通过施工区的车辆比例下降6至90个百分点，经典规划器下降18至19个百分点，且所有学习策略的近碰撞情况更频繁。

items.title: SceneFactory-3D: Lifting 2D Traffic Scenes into 3D Physical Counterfactuals for Scalable Physically Grounded Safety Evaluation

items.intro: arXiv:2610.03388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video is an abundant, inexpensive source of human motion data that is rich in extreme athletic behaviors. Making it usable for humanoid robots, however, is not a matter of simply retargeting a reconstructed trajectory: video-derived motion is physically inconsistent, devoid of actuation information, and says nothing about failure or recovery. We present KungfuAthleteBot (KAB), a framework that treats learning high-dynamic motion from video as the central problem and resolves each of these three

sections.text:
Video is an abundant, inexpensive source of human motion data that is rich in extreme athletic behaviors. Making it usable for humanoid robots, however, is not a matter of simply retargeting a reconstructed trajectory: video-derived motion is physically inconsistent, devoid of actuation information, and says nothing about failure or recovery.

We present KungfuAthleteBot (KAB), a framework that treats learning high-dynamic motion from video as the central problem and resolves each of these three failure modes in turn. (C1) We build the KungfuAthlete dataset from videos of national-level martial artists and introduce a physics-guided parabolic trajectory correction that removes height floating, ground penetration, and high-frequency jitter from reconstructed aerial and landing phases. (C2) Because video carries no force information, strict tracking of a reconstructed trajectory is dynamically infeasible, and error-driven initialization keeps re-launching the policy from infeasible aerial poses.

We introduce physics-driven pseudo-low-kinetic-energy (LKE) sampling, our central mechanism for making such references learnable: it biases initialization towards dynamically feasible states, letting the policy discover feasible actuation patterns instead of imitating infeasible ones. (C3) Finally, we introduce a direct training paradigm in which disturbance rejection and fall recovery are learned inside the same policy that tracks the video motion, requiring no recovery reference data and no manual mode switching.

On a humanoid robot, KAB learns dynamic skills from video and recovers from arbitrary falls in about 0.7 s, the fastest reported recovery for a unified policy.

Ablations on the unified policy confirm the necessity of its components, supporting the view that repairing and compensating video data, rather than only collecting more of it, is what unlocks high-dynamic humanoid skills.

summary.en: The paper presents KungfuAthleteBot (KAB), a framework for learning high-dynamic humanoid skills from martial-arts video. Its dataset contains videos of national-level martial artists, and physics-guided parabolic correction addresses floating, ground penetration, and jitter in reconstructed aerial and landing motions. Pseudo-low-kinetic-energy sampling favors feasible initial states, while a unified policy learns motion tracking, disturbance rejection, and fall recovery. The authors report recovery from arbitrary falls in about 0.7 seconds on a humanoid robot, which they describe as the fastest reported recovery for a unified policy. Ablations support the components’ necessity.
summary.zh: 论文提出 KungfuAthleteBot（KAB），从武术视频学习高动态人形机器人动作。作者构建了包含国家级武术运动员视频的数据集，并用物理引导的抛物线轨迹修正处理重建动作中的漂浮、穿地和抖动。为解决视频缺少力信息导致的动作不可行问题，方法通过伪低动能采样选择更可行的初始化状态，并在同一策略中学习动作跟踪、抗扰和跌倒恢复。作者报告机器人可从任意跌倒中约0.7秒恢复，并称这是统一策略中报告最快的恢复速度；消融实验支持各组件的必要性。

items.title: KungfuAthleteBot: learning high-dynamic humanoid motion from video with unified robust recovery

items.intro: arXiv:2608.23927v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video generative models provide rich physical priors for robot learning, yet existing world-action models (WAMs) face a fundamental trade-off: synchronous video generation at control rate is latency-prohibitive, while abandoning test-time visual imagination sacrifices task success.
